name: Barbiecore
eras: massive 2022–2023 peak tied to the Barbie film

media.title: Barbie (2023 film, dir. Greta Gerwig)
media.note: the single largest driver of the 2022-23 peak, including a widely reported global shortage of the specific pink paint used on marketing materials

media.title: Valentino's 2022 Pink PP collection
media.note: the fashion-world moment that preceded and fed into the film's marketing wave

reacts_against: the muted, 'quiet luxury' neutral palettes dominant in mid-2010s fashion; Barbiecore is maximalist, loud and unambiguous about embracing a color long coded as frivolous.
revivals: already a recurring micro-trend since the 1990s before 2022's major peak
article: Barbiecore's palette has a corporate paint code behind it. The 2023 Barbie film's marketing campaign used a specific, extremely saturated magenta-leaning pink so consistently and at such scale that it reportedly contributed to a real-world shortage of one particular Rosco paint shade among Hollywood suppliers — a detail that says something true about this aesthetic: it isn't a loose family of similar pinks, it's closer to one exact, brand-defined hue worn as totally as possible, head to toe, with almost nothing allowed to dilute it. That single-mindedness has precedent well before 2023; fashion had already flirted with all-pink maximalism in Valentino's widely covered 2022 collection, and Barbiecore itself had surfaced as a minor recurring trend since at least the 1990s, whenever fashion wanted to reclaim a color still carrying decades of "frivolous" and "juvenile" coding and wear that coding on purpose, at full volume. What made the film's version different was scale: a marketing budget large enough to put that one pink on billboards, red carpets and plastic merchandise simultaneously, turning a fashion micro-trend into a genuinely global color moment for most of a year.
